title: General privileges on HF
summary: Only four HF bands have portions General cannot use. On 10 meters, General may send CW across the entire band.

points.label: General on 15 meters
points.value: 21300 kHz is in the General portion

hook: Start at 80 and halve: 80, 40, 20, then 15. Those four have Extra-only gaps. 10 meters CW: the entire band.

title: Power limits: one big number
summary: Power is measured as PEP output. Most bands asked about allow 1500 W; learn the two smaller numbers as exceptions.
hook: Mostly big (1500 W), smaller on 30 m (200 W), tiny for spread spectrum (10 W).

title: Special rules on 30 m and 60 m
summary: Two odd bands with their own rules: 30 meters bans voice and pictures, 60 meters limits bandwidth and asks for an antenna record.

points.label: 60 meters, non-dipole
points.value: Keep a record of your antenna gain

hook: 30 m: no phone, no image. 60 m: USB up to 2.8 kHz, and log the gain of any antenna that is not a dipole.

title: Beacon stations at a glance
summary: Beacons exist so hams can observe propagation. A few rules cover where, how many and how strong.

points.label: How many
points.value: No more than one per band, same location

title: Volunteer Examiner rules
summary: VEs are accredited by a VEC and must be 18. A General class VE can give only the Technician exam.

points.label: Non-US citizen VE
points.value: FCC license, General class or above

points.label: Observing a Tech exam
points.value: At least three VEs, General or higher

hook: General keeps showing up: a non-US citizen VE needs General or above, and a Tech exam needs three General or higher VEs.

title: Upgrade credit: CSCEs and old licenses
summary: A CSCE lets you use new privileges right away. An old license can still earn credit, with conditions.

points.label: Until the database updates
points.value: Add AG when using General privileges

points.label: Partial credit, expired
points.value: Once held General, Advanced or Extra

points.label: Past the 2 year grace
points.value: Show the old license, pass Element 2

hook: A CSCE is good for 365 days. Sign AG while you use General privileges before the upgrade shows up.

title: Third-party messages: who, what, how
summary: Three questions about third-party traffic: who is disqualified, what may be said, and whether remote control changes anything.

points.label: What may be sent
points.value: Amateur radio, personal, emergency or disaster

points.label: Via remote control
points.value: Whenever FCC rules permit third party

title: Which sideband: upper, with exceptions
summary: HF voice is single sideband. Upper sideband is the rule; lower sideband is the custom on the low bands and for RTTY.

points.label: Why LSB there
points.value: It is commonly accepted amateur practice

hook: Upper is the rule. Lower is the exception: the 160, 75 and 40 meter bands by custom, and RTTY.

title: Why SSB is efficient, and louder
summary: SSB throws away what it does not need, then a speech processor squeezes more average power from what is left.

points.label: What SSB sends
points.value: One sideband only; carrier also suppressed

points.label: Speech processor goal
points.value: More apparent loudness of your voice

title: Spacing by mode: hertz to kilohertz
summary: Three small spans to know: the RTTY shift, and the gap to leave beside CW and SSB signals.
hook: Wider signal, wider gap: CW needs hundreds of hertz, SSB needs 2 to 3 kHz.

title: FT8 on 20 meters
summary: FT8 sits inside the 20 meter digital segment and runs on strict timing.
hook: Nested ranges: FT8 at 14.074 to 14.077 sits inside the digital segment, 14.070 to 14.100.

title: Q signals family
summary: Every Q signal is three letters starting with Q, and each one stands for a whole sentence.

points.label: QRL?
points.value: Are you busy? Is this frequency in use?

points.label: Before calling CQ
points.value: CW: send QRL? Phone: ask. Then your call

title: CW endings and report add-ons
summary: Short CW signals at the end of a message or report carry a specific meaning.

title: Calling, answering, breaking in
summary: Each way of joining the air has its own etiquette. DX means stations outside the lower 48 states.

points.label: Calling CQ on HF
points.value: Repeat CQ, then this is and your call

points.label: Answering CQ on CW
points.value: Comfortable copy speed, no faster than CQ

points.label: CQ DX from the lower 48
points.value: Answer only if outside the lower 48

points.label: 50.1 to 50.125 MHz
points.value: Only contacts outside the 48 contiguous states

hook: DX means outside the lower 48: the same idea for a CQ DX call and for 50.1 to 50.125 MHz.

title: Emergencies and RACES
summary: Normally no one owns a frequency. Emergencies come first, and RACES has its own rules.

points.label: Distress station breaks in
points.value: Acknowledge it, find what help is needed

points.label: Routine RACES drills
points.value: No more than 1 hour per week

title: Digital messaging: Winlink and friends
summary: Winlink messages pass through gateway stations. VARA and PACTOR are digital protocols; AREDN is a mesh network.

points.label: VARA
points.value: A digital protocol used with Winlink

points.label: Reaching a gateway
points.value: Connect message on its published frequency

points.label: AREDN mesh network
points.value: High-speed data in emergencies or events

title: Volunteer Monitors: what, why, how
summary: A volunteer program for keeping the bands clean: who they are, what they aim for, and one technique they use.

points.label: What
points.value: Volunteers enlisted to monitor for violations

points.label: Find a stuck carrier
points.value: Compare beam headings with other monitors

title: Short path and long path
summary: A signal can go the short way or the long way around the Earth, and the map and antenna heading follow from that.

points.label: Azimuthal projection map
points.value: True bearings and distances from one spot

points.label: Both paths at once
points.value: A slightly delayed echo might be heard

title: Solar events by arrival time
summary: Order solar effects by how fast they reach Earth, then add the Sun's own rotation cycle.

points.label: 26 to 28 day cycle
points.value: Rotation of the Sun's surface layers

hook: Minutes, then hours to days, then weeks: flare radiation, a CME, and the Sun turning once.

title: Space weather yardsticks
summary: One number measures solar radiation; two indexes measure how steady Earth's magnetic field is.

points.label: Geomagnetic storm
points.value: Temporary disturbance in the geomagnetic field

hook: K and A are a pair: K is short-term, A is long-term.

title: How the Sun shapes the bands
summary: More sunspots help the high bands. Disturbances hurt: sudden disturbances hit lower frequencies, geomagnetic storms hit high latitudes.

points.label: Higher sunspot numbers
points.value: Better odds of good high-frequency propagation

points.label: 20 m worldwide by day
points.value: At any point in the solar cycle

points.label: Sudden disturbance, daytime
points.value: Hurts lower frequencies more than higher

points.label: High geomagnetic activity
points.value: Auroras that can reflect VHF signals

title: The MUF and LUF window
summary: Skywave works in a window between two limits. Below it, signals are absorbed. Inside it, they come back to Earth.

points.label: MUF
points.value: Maximum Usable Frequency between two points

points.label: LUF
points.value: Lowest Usable Frequency between two points

points.label: LUF above the MUF
points.value: No ordinary skywave on that path

hook: Picture a window: the LUF is the sill, the MUF is the top. Aim just under the top. No window, no skywave.

title: Ionosphere regions, bottom to top
summary: The lowest region absorbs by day. Higher regions bend signals back, and the higher the region, the longer the hop.

points.label: 40, 60, 80, 160 m by day
points.value: Hard: the D region absorbs them

hook: Climb the layers: D absorbs by day, E hops about 1,200 miles, F2 (the highest) about 2,500.

title: The two criticals, and NVIS
summary: Both critical values are a highest limit for a signal to return to Earth. NVIS uses high angles on purpose.

points.label: Critical frequency
points.value: Highest frequency refracted back to Earth

points.label: Critical angle
points.value: Highest takeoff angle that returns to Earth

points.label: NVIS
points.value: Short distance MF/HF at high elevation angles

hook: Critical means highest: the highest frequency, or the highest angle, that still comes back down.

title: Scatter into the skip zone
summary: Scatter lets you hear stations in the skip zone, but only a little energy arrives, over many paths.

points.label: Why weak
points.value: Only a small part of the energy gets there

title: Decibels and link math
summary: Decibels turn multiplying into adding. 3 dB is a factor of two in power.

points.label: Link budget
points.value: Transmit power plus antenna gains minus losses

points.label: Link margin
points.value: Received level minus minimum required level

hook: Because dB values add, a link budget is just power plus gains minus losses, as seen at the receiver.

title: S meter steps in decibels
summary: An S meter shows received signal strength. Each S unit is a fixed step in dB, so readings convert to power ratios.

points.label: S8 to S9 at the far end

hook: One S unit is 6 dB, about 4 times the power. 20 dB over S9 is 100 times.

title: Where a 3 kHz sideband signal sits
summary: A sideband signal spreads to one side of the displayed carrier: LSB below it, USB above it. Keep that side clear of the edge.

points.label: LSB near lower edge
points.value: At least 3 kHz above the edge

points.label: USB near upper edge
points.value: At least 3 kHz below the edge

hook: Lower sideband hangs 3 kHz below the dial, upper sideband 3 kHz above it.

title: Receiver tools: match fix to problem
summary: Each receiver control targets one kind of trouble. Learn the trouble each one fixes.

points.label: Notch filter
points.value: Cuts carriers in the receiver passband

points.label: Noise blanker
points.value: Reduces receiver gain during a noise pulse

points.label: Dual VFO
points.value: Transmit on one frequency, listen on another

title: Amplifier tuning and ALC
summary: Tune the amplifier for a dip, load it for power within limits, and let ALC guard against overdrive except on data.

points.label: Tube amp TUNE control
points.value: A pronounced dip in plate current

points.label: LOAD or COUPLING control
points.value: Desired power, not over max plate current

points.label: Setting ALC on SSB
points.value: Adjust transmit audio or mic gain

points.label: ALC with AFSK data
points.value: Keep it inactive: ALC distorts the signal

points.label: Delay before RF output
points.value: Lets the amp switch the antenna over

title: Oscilloscope and the two-tone test
summary: The oscilloscope shows waveforms, not just numbers, so it is the tool for keying and RF envelope checks.

points.label: RF envelope, vertical input
points.value: Attenuated RF output of the transmitter

title: Meters and analyzers: which for what
summary: Digital for precision, analog for peaking, wattmeters and analyzers for SWR and impedance.

points.label: Analog multimeter
points.value: Adjusting for maximum or minimum values

points.label: Voltmeter, high impedance
points.value: Less loading on the circuit measured

title: RF interference: sound and fix
summary: What the interference sounds like points to its source; a capacitor or choke is often the cure.

points.label: Across many frequencies
points.value: Arcing at a poor electrical connection

points.label: Common-mode on audio cable
points.value: Place a ferrite choke on the cable

hook: The noise copies the mode: SSB sounds like garbled speech, CW like on-and-off hums or clicks.

title: Grounding and bonding: problem and fix
summary: Bonding enclosures together fixes ground loops and hot spots. A ground wire must not be resonant or high impedance.

points.label: Why ground enclosures
points.value: No hazardous voltages on the chassis

points.label: Ground loop symptom
points.value: Reports of hum on your transmitted signal

points.label: Cause of RF burns
points.value: Ground wire has high impedance on that frequency

points.label: Resonant ground
points.value: High RF voltages on equipment enclosures

points.label: Lightning ground joints
points.value: Not soldered: lightning heat destroys them

hook: Loops and hot spots have one answer: bond the enclosures together.

title: HF mobile: short antennas, heavy wires
summary: A mobile antenna is electrically short, which limits efficiency and bandwidth. Power comes straight from the battery.

points.label: Biggest limit
points.value: Efficiency of the electrically short antenna

points.label: Shortened antenna drawback
points.value: Operating bandwidth may be very limited

points.label: Corona ball
points.value: Reduces RF discharge from the tip

points.label: Not the aux power socket
points.value: Its wiring may not handle the current

title: Solar charging, cell to battery
summary: Follow the power from one cell, through the panel, past a diode and controller, into the battery.

points.label: Series diode
points.value: Stops battery discharge through the panel

points.label: Lithium iron phosphate
points.value: Panel must have a charge controller

title: Reactance and impedance
summary: Reactance is how coils and capacitors resist AC. They react to frequency in opposite directions.

points.label: What reactance is
points.value: Opposition to AC from capacitance or inductance

points.label: Impedance
points.value: The ratio of voltage to current

hook: Coils and capacitors are opposites: raise the frequency and an inductor fights harder, a capacitor gives way.

title: Resonance and oscillators
summary: At resonance the coil's and capacitor's reactances are equal and cancel. That one frequency is what an LC oscillator runs at.

points.label: LC oscillator frequency
points.value: Set by L and C in the tank circuit

points.label: Sine wave oscillator parts
points.value: A filter and an amplifier in a feedback loop

title: Series vs parallel
summary: Inductors combine like resistors. Capacitors do the opposite: they add in parallel and combine like reciprocals in series.

points.label: Parallel branch currents
points.value: Total current is the sum of the branches

hook: To grow an inductor, add one in series. To grow a capacitor, add one in parallel. The reciprocal rule always lands below the smallest part.

title: Three power formulas
summary: Know any two of volts, amps and ohms and one formula gives the power.

points.label: 400 V across 800 ohms
points.value: P = E x E / R = 200 watts

points.label: 7.0 mA through 1,250 ohms
points.value: P = I x I x R, about 61 milliwatts

points.label: 1200 W into 50 ohms
points.value: E = square root of P x R: 245 volts

hook: Watch the units: milliamps in gives milliwatts out (7.0 mA gives 61 milliwatts, not 61 watts).

title: Peak, RMS and PEP
summary: RMS is the heating value of AC. Peak x 0.707 gives RMS, and peak to peak is twice the peak.

points.label: RMS value
points.value: Same heating in a resistor as that DC voltage

hook: For PEP: halve the peak to peak to get peak, times 0.707 for RMS, then square it and divide by the load (50 ohms).

title: Transformers and matching
summary: A transformer trades voltage for current by its turns ratio, which also lets it match one impedance to another.

points.label: Step-up primary wire
points.value: Larger, for the higher primary current

points.label: Matching transformer at rig
points.value: Presents the desired impedance to rig and line

hook: Volts follow the turns ratio. Impedance follows its square: 600 / 50 is 12, and 3.5 x 3.5 is about 12.

title: Passive parts and their quirks
summary: Each passive part has a strength and a hidden side that shows up at radio frequencies.

points.label: Electrolytic capacitor
points.value: High capacitance for a given volume

points.label: Ferrite core performance
points.value: Set by the mix of materials

points.label: Ferrite toroid inductor
points.value: Large inductance, contained field, tuned core

points.label: Ferrite bead on coax
points.value: Adds impedance in the common-mode path

hook: Resistors hide inductance and inductors turn capacitive up high. Ferrite works by adding impedance, chosen by its mix.

title: Diodes, transistors and tubes
summary: Each active device has one key fact: the voltage it turns on at, how it is biased, or which part controls the flow.

points.label: MOSFET gate
points.value: Thin insulating layer separates it from channel

points.label: Tube control grid
points.value: Regulates electron flow, cathode to plate

hook: Germanium 0.3 plus silicon 0.7 adds up to 1 volt. A switch lives at the two extremes: fully on (saturation) or fully off (cutoff).

title: Integrated circuit types
summary: Three kinds of integrated circuit, one key fact each: analog op amps, low-power CMOS, microwave MMICs.

title: Connectors by frequency
summary: Pick a connector by how high the signal goes, from RCA for dc up to type N at 10 GHz.

points.label: BNC, 50 ohm
points.value: Low SWR up to about 4 GHz

points.label: SMA
points.value: Small, threaded, signals up to several GHz

hook: Climbing the ladder: RCA for dc, BNC to 4 GHz, N to 10 GHz and weatherproof.

title: Power supply building blocks
summary: AC goes in, a rectifier flips it to pulses of DC, a filter smooths them, and a bleeder makes it safe after shutoff.

points.label: Half-wave rectifier
points.value: One diode, 180 degrees of the cycle

points.label: Full-wave rectifier
points.value: Two diodes and a center-tapped transformer

points.label: Full-wave output
points.value: 360 degrees, pulses at twice the AC frequency

points.label: Bleeder resistor
points.value: Discharges filter capacitors after power off

hook: Half-wave uses half the cycle (180 degrees), full-wave the whole cycle (360 degrees), so full-wave pulses come twice as often.

title: Figure G7-1 symbol map
summary: Figure G7-1 numbers each symbol. Learn the five the pool asks about.
hook: Transistors come first (1 and 2), the Zener diode is 5, and the coils sit together at 6 and 7.

title: Amplifier classes
summary: Amplifier classes trade faithfulness for efficiency, from Class A that conducts all the time to efficient Class C.

points.label: Efficiency
points.value: RF output power divided by DC input power

hook: Class A is on 100% of the time. Class C wins on efficiency and suits FM, not SSB or AM.

title: Digital building blocks
summary: Three basic digital circuits: a gate makes decisions, a counter counts states, a shift register moves data.

points.label: Two-input AND gate
points.value: Output high only when both inputs are high

points.label: Shift register
points.value: Clocked array passing data in steps

hook: Each bit doubles the count: 3 bits give 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 states.

title: Filter vocabulary
summary: A filter's edges are its half-power points. Inside, you measure the loss; outside, the rejection.

points.label: Band-pass bandwidth
points.value: Between upper and lower half-power points

hook: Inside the passband: insertion loss. Outside it: ultimate rejection. The edges: half power.

title: SSB signal path
summary: SSB is made in two steps and recovered in one: make double sideband, filter away one side, then detect.

points.label: Product detector
points.value: In an SSB receiver, extracts the signal

title: Software-defined and DSP radios
summary: In an SDR, software does the radio's work, built on I and Q signals.

points.label: DSP filter advantage
points.value: Wide range of bandwidths and shapes

title: What each modulation changes
summary: Every modulation changes one property of the RF wave: its power, its frequency or its phase.

title: What sets signal bandwidth
summary: Bandwidth grows with deviation, symbol rate and overdriving. Match the receiver to it.

points.label: Receiver bandwidth
points.value: Match the mode for best signal-to-noise

points.label: Flat-topping
points.value: Distortion from too much drive or speech

points.label: Waterfall display axes
points.value: Frequency across, time down, strength intensity

points.label: Waterfall vertical lines
points.value: Overmodulation of data or RTTY signal

hook: FM bandwidth is 2 x (deviation + audio): 2 x (5 + 3) = 16 kHz. Overmodulation shows as excess width: vertical lines on a waterfall.

title: Mixers and multipliers
summary: A mixer outputs sum and difference frequencies. A multiplier makes harmonics, multiplying deviation too.

points.label: Mixer output
points.value: Sum and difference of LO and RF

hook: The multiplier scales deviation too: 146.52 / 12.21 = 12, so 5 kHz / 12 = 416.7 Hz at the oscillator.

title: Intermodulation order
summary: Nonlinear mixing makes unwanted products. The odd-order ones land closest to the real signals.
hook: Add the multipliers to get the order: 2F1-F2 is 2 + 1 = 3, odd.

title: FSK, PSK and their codes
summary: FSK shifts between two frequencies, PSK shifts phase. Each pairs with a character code.

points.label: Baudot code
points.value: 5-bit code plus start and stop bits

points.label: QPSK31
points.value: Sideband sensitive, error correcting, BPSK width

hook: Quad means four: QPSK uses four phases, so each shift carries a pair of bits.

title: Weak-signal and digital voice modes
summary: Each of these digital modes has one job: beacons, weak-signal contacts, or voice.

points.label: FT8 report of +3
points.value: Signal-to-noise +3 dB in a 2.5 kHz bandwidth

hook: FT8 has 8 in its name and 8 tones in its signal.

title: Getting data through intact
summary: Digital links protect data two ways: ask again when something fails, or send extra so the receiver can fix it.

points.label: Mesh node fails
points.value: Packet can go via an alternate node

title: Feed line basics
summary: Feed line loss is counted in dB per length and rises with frequency. Spacing sets a parallel line's impedance.

points.label: Parallel line impedance
points.value: Set by conductor spacing and radius

title: SWR and mismatch
summary: SWR comes from a mismatch between feed line and antenna. A tuner hides it from the rig but the line still sees it.

points.label: Cause of reflected power
points.value: Feed line and feed point impedances differ

points.label: Prevent standing waves
points.value: Match feed point to line impedance

points.label: High SWR
points.value: Increases loss in a lossy line

points.label: Higher line loss
points.value: Lowers SWR measured at the line input

hook: SWR is the larger impedance over the smaller: 200 / 50 = 4, and 50 / 10 = 5.

title: Antenna length vs frequency
summary: Lower frequency means a longer antenna. Length goes opposite to frequency.
hook: 3.550 MHz is about 1/4 of 14.250 MHz, so its dipole is 4 times longer: 33 feet x 4 = 132 feet.

title: Radiation pattern shapes
summary: Each antenna shape has a signature pattern. Learn where each one radiates and where it goes quiet.

points.label: Main lobe
points.value: Direction of maximum radiated field strength

points.label: Front-to-back ratio
points.value: Major lobe power vs the opposite direction

points.label: Dipole in free space
points.value: Figure-eight at right angles to the wire

points.label: VHF/UHF halo
points.value: Omnidirectional in the plane of the halo

title: Dipole height and feed point
summary: A dipole's impedance and pattern shift with height and with where you feed it.
hook: Impedance climbs from the center toward the ends, so feeding right at the end is very high.

title: Verticals and ground
summary: Vertical antennas depend on their radials and the ground beneath them.

points.label: Ground-mounted radials
points.value: On the surface or a few inches under

hook: Radials go down: sloped downward when raised, on or just under the soil when ground-mounted.

title: Yagi design and matching
summary: A Yagi is a driven element with a longer reflector and shorter directors. Its dimensions trade gain, pattern and bandwidth.

points.label: Two stacked 1/2 wave apart
points.value: About 3 dB more, lobe narrower in elevation

points.label: Beta or hairpin match
points.value: Shorted stub at the feed point

points.label: Gamma match
points.value: Driven element need not be insulated

hook: Lengths step down: reflector longer, driven element about 1/2 wave, director shorter.

title: Special-purpose antennas
summary: Each specialty antenna is known for one strength or one weakness.

points.label: Beverage antenna
points.value: Directional receiving, MF and low HF

title: RF exposure: what counts
summary: RF heats tissue. Exposure depends on power density, frequency and duty cycle, averaged over time.

points.label: Factors in exposure
points.value: Duty cycle, frequency and power density

points.label: Time averaging
points.value: Total exposure averaged over a period

hook: Time averaging is why duty cycle matters: transmit less of the time and you may use more power.

title: RF exposure: the steps
summary: Evaluate your station, then keep people out of any area that is over the limit.

points.label: Fail the exemption
points.value: RF evaluation per FCC OET Bulletin 65

points.label: Accurate field measurement
points.value: Calibrated meter with a calibrated antenna

points.label: Routine duty
points.value: Evaluate and block high exposure areas

points.label: Over the limit
points.value: Prevent human exposure to those fields

points.label: Neighbor in the main lobe
points.value: Ensure it cannot point at them while present

points.label: Indoor antenna
points.value: MPE limits not exceeded in occupied areas

title: Station wiring safety
summary: The National Electrical Code covers station safety: size wire to the breaker and protect only the hot wires.

points.label: GFCI trips on
points.value: Current from hot directly to ground

points.label: Power supply interlock
points.value: Removes dangerous voltage if cabinet opens

hook: Lower AWG number, bigger breaker: AWG 14 goes with 15 A, AWG 12 with 20 A.

title: Lightning protection layout
summary: Keep lightning outside: ground outside, arrestors at the entry, and every ground tied together.

points.label: Lightning arrestors
points.value: Where feed lines enter the building

points.label: Ground rods
points.value: Bonded together with all other grounds
